newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Koncar aims at six pct return - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Koncar aims at six pct return - paper.

text.p: Croatian electrical concern Koncar Elektroindustrija, which plans to float 30 percent of its shares abroad within a year, said on Wednesday it was planning to boost profits to over six percent.
Koncar's chief executive Vjekoslav Srb said in an interview with Zagreb daily Vjesnik that the company had more than doubled its productivity since 1994, due to a tough restructuring programme.
Koncar on Tuesday signed an agreement with Zagrebacka Banka and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to help it float 31.16 percent of its capital on the international market.
"Our basic goal is to reach a minimum of six percent return on the capital, and we are also planning a dynamic boost of sales," Srb said.
He singled out the production of electric generators and other equipment for production and transfer of energy as the main area in which Koncar expects fastest growth in future.

Koncar is planning to invest some 340 million kuna in new technology in the next five years, following several years in which it refrained from borrowing due to high interest rates on the Croatian financial markets.

The heavily export-oriented group, which consists of more than 60 smaller companies, recorded a one-percent fall in exports in the first five months of the year, but compensated for it by an 11-percent increase in sales on the domestic market.
Srb said the average productivity per employee rose from 25,000 German marks in 1994, to around 70,000 marks in 1997, as the result of the restructuring programme.
The programme combined shedding surplus labour with letting some of the loss-making subsidiaries of the group go bankrupt.
Srb said he did not foresee any radical cuts in the future after the recent bankruptcy of Koncar-Dizala elevator producer.
Koncar is valued at 365 million marks, and is owned by state funds, except for small stakes held by German electrical giant Siemens and employees.
Its 1996 sales topped one million kuna, 30 percent of which were exports.
